questions.stem:
The random variable $X \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$

Given that $\mathrm{P}(X>\mu+a)=0.35$ where $a$ is a constant, find

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: $\mathrm{P}(X>\mu-a)=\underline{0.65}$
NB you may see $\mathrm{P}(Z<0.35)=0.6368$ which is of course B0

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) M1: $\mathrm{P}(\mu-a<X<\mu+a)=1-2\times0.35$ or "0.65" $-0.35$ or $0.15+0.15$, ft their answer to part (a) [M0 for a probability $<0$]
A1: $=\underline{0.3}$ (Answer only scores both marks)

parts.label: c
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: $\mathrm{P}(X<\mu+a \mid X>\mu-a)=\dfrac{\text{"(b)"}}{\text{"(a)"}}=\dfrac{0.3}{0.65}$ for a correct ratio of probabilities or follow through their answers provided (b) < (a)
A1: $=\dfrac{6}{13}$ (Allow awrt 0.462) or an exact equivalent and allow awrt 0.462

questions.stem:
Hugo recorded the purchases of 80 customers in the ladies fashion department of a large store. His results were as follows

20 customers bought a coat
12 customers bought a coat and a scarf
23 customers bought a pair of gloves
13 customers bought a pair of gloves and a scarf
no customer bought a coat and a pair of gloves
14 customers did not buy a coat nor a scarf nor a pair of gloves.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a Venn diagram to represent all of this information.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) B1: for 3 labelled circles with 12, 13 & $n(C \cap G)=0$ marked or implied (e.g.RH diagram)
B1: for 8 and 10 correctly placed
B1: for 23 correctly placed
B1: for box 14
May use probabilities not integers. A blank space does not imply a zero

parts.label: b(i)
parts.text:
(b) One of the 80 customers is selected at random.

(i) Find the probability that the customer bought a scarf.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b)(i) B1ft: $\mathrm{P}(S)=\left[\dfrac{12+23+13}{80}\right]=\dfrac{48}{80}$ or $\dfrac{3}{5}$ or $0.6$, for 0.6 or any exact equivalent (single fraction) or ft their values
Official notes (completeness pass):
- B1ft for 0.6 or any exact equivalent (single fraction) or ft their values (ft blank as 0)

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.text:
(ii) Given that the customer bought a coat, find the probability that the customer also bought a scarf.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b)(ii) M1: $\mathrm{P}(S\mid C)=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(S\cap C)}{\mathrm{P}(C)}=\dfrac{12/80}{20/80}$, for a correct conditional prob. Correct expression and one correct ft prob. Num < Den
A1cso: $=\dfrac{12}{20}$ or $\underline{0.6}$, for 0.6 which must come from a denominator of 20

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.text:
(iii) State, giving a reason, whether or not the event 'the customer bought a coat' and the event 'the customer bought a scarf' are statistically independent.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b)(iii) B1ft: $\mathrm{P}(S)=\mathrm{P}(S\mid C)$ or $\mathrm{P}(C)=0.25$, $\mathrm{P}(C\cap S)=0.15$ and $\mathrm{P}(C)\times\mathrm{P}(S)=0.6\times0.25$, for a full reason. If not $\mathrm{P}(S)=\mathrm{P}(S\mid C)$ then all values must be stated, labelled and correct or correct ft from diagram. Correct not'n required so $\mathrm{P}(S\cup C)=0.15$ is B0B0
dB1ft: so $S$ and $C$ are independent, dependent on a correct reason for correct conclusion for their values

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Hugo had asked the member of staff selling coats and the member of staff selling gloves to encourage customers also to buy a scarf.

(c) By considering suitable conditional probabilities, determine whether the member of staff selling coats or the member of staff selling gloves has the better performance at selling scarves to their customers. Give a reason for your answer.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1: Need $\mathrm{P}(S\mid G)=\dfrac{13}{23}$, for attempt at $\mathrm{P}(S\mid G)$ correct ratio of probabilities or numbers using their figs
A1: for $\dfrac{13}{23}$ (accept awrt 0.565) [Sight of $\mathrm{P}(S\mid G)=\dfrac{13}{23}$ is M1A1]
A1: $\mathrm{P}(S\mid C)=0.6>0.565$ so assistant selling coats has the better performance, for a correct conclusion that chooses "coats" based on a correct comparison. Allow incorrect $\mathrm{P}(S\mid C)$ provided > 0.565 to score 2nd A1 and so all 3 marks. Condone poor use of notation eg S|G with no P(..). Probabilities may be described in words. Condone comparison of $\dfrac{13}{23}$ with 0.6 even if $\dfrac{13}{23}$ is not labelled as $\mathrm{P}(S\mid G)$

questions.stem:
The stem and leaf diagram gives the blood pressure, $x$ mmHg, for a random sample of 19 female patients.

$\begin{array}{c|ccccccccc}10 & 1 & 2 & & & & & & & (2)\\11 & 2 & 7 & 7 & 8 & 8 & & & & (5)\\12 & 0 & 2 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 4 & 5 & 5 & 7\ (9)\\13 & 1 & 2 & 9 & & & & & & (3)\end{array}$

Key: 10 | 1 means blood pressure of 101 mmHg

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the median and the quartiles for these data.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme: (a) B1B1B1: $Q_1=117$, $Q_2=122$, $Q_3=125$, for all 3 correct, B1B1B0 for any 2 correct and B1B0B0 for only one correct

parts.label: b
parts.mark_scheme: (b) B1ft: $\mathrm{IQR}=125-117=\underline{8}$, for their greatest value from (a) minus their smallest value from (a)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
An outlier is a value that is greater than $Q_3+1.5\times(Q_3-Q_1)$ or less than $Q_1-1.5\times(Q_3-Q_1)$

(c) Showing your working clearly, identify any outliers for these data.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) M1A1: Upper limit: $125+1.5\times8=125+12=\underline{137}$, Lower limit: $117-12=\underline{105}$, for a correct expression for either limit, ft their values; 1st A1 for both 137 and 105 identified
A1ft: Outliers are: $\underline{101}$, $\underline{102}$ and $\underline{139}$, for correctly identifying all the outliers using their limits. Must have scored M1. This 2nd A1ft can be awarded if all the outliers are seen on the box plot in (d)

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) On the grid on page 21 draw a box and whisker plot to represent these data. Show any outliers clearly.
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
(d) M1: for a box and two whiskers (Must be on the grid, otherwise 0/4)
A1ft: for $Q_1, Q_2$ and $Q_3$ all plotted correctly, ft their values from (a)
B1: for lower whisker plotted at 105 or 112 and outliers at 101 and 102
B1: for upper whisker plotted at 137 or 132 and an outlier at 139 (Whiskers must be compatible e.g. if lower whisker is at 105 upper must be at 137)

parts.label: e
parts.text:
The above data can be summarised by

$\sum x=2299$ and $\sum x^2=279709$

(e) Calculate the mean and the standard deviation for these data.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(e) B1: $[\bar{x}=]\underline{121}$
M1: $[\sigma_x=]\sqrt{\dfrac{279709}{19}-\bar{x}^2}=\sqrt{14721.526...-14641}=\sqrt{80.526...}$, for a correct expression including square root, ft their mean
A1: $=\text{awrt }\underline{8.97}$ (Allow $s=9.2195...$ or awrt 9.22)

parts.label: f
parts.text:
For a random sample taken from a normal distribution, a rule for determining outliers is:

an outlier is more than $2.7 \times$ standard deviation above or below the mean.

(f) Find the limits to determine outliers using this rule.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(f) M1: for an attempt to calculate one limit, ft their mean and s.d.
A1: $\bar{x}+2.7\times\sigma_x=\text{awrt }\underline{145}$, $\bar{x}-2.7\times\sigma_x=\text{awrt }\underline{96.8}$ (allow 97), for both limits correct allow awrt 145 and awrt 96.8 or 97

parts.label: g
parts.text:
(g) State, giving a reason based on some of the above calculations, whether or not a normal distribution is a suitable model for these data.
(1)
parts.mark_scheme: (g) B1: Probably not suitable...since: data is skewed or (f) says no outliers, (c) says 3, or (a) says median = 122, (e) says mean = 121, for stating, or implying, normal not suitable and giving at least one supporting reason. A calculation or description of skewness is not required but if present must be correct for their values or their box plot. "Not normal since data is not continuous" is B0
